The four bytes were re-read out of the image for this package rather than taken from the committed listing, because at this length the listing has nothing to cross-check against. implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX and nothing else. There are zero ordinary stack arguments, which is not an omission: the terminator at 0x005c0dd3 is a bare RET with no immediate, the body contains no read of ESP and no read of any [EBP+k] frame slot, and abi_derived.stack_arguments records observed_slots 0, derived_slots 0, gaps 0, total_bytes 0 with cleanup {bytes 0, side caller, evidence 'ret with no immediate, no stack reads'}. The model test MEASURES this rather than asserting the convention: it pushes a decoy word, calls through a trampoline, and requires ESP after the return to sit exactly four bytes below where it was, which is what a zero-byte callee cleanup looks like and is not what a `RET 4` reconstruction produces.
implementation.return_type_rationale: The machine fixes a WIDTH of one byte and nothing more. The destination operand of 8A is AL, so exactly one byte is written into the return register, and that is the whole width claim. The C++ spelling is a source-side choice among bool, unsigned char and std::uint8_t, all of which compile to these same three bytes; std::uint8_t is declared because it is the least committal of the three. bool is specifically NOT claimed: a bool return would assert the value is {0, 1}, and nothing in these two instructions masks anything -- the byte at 0x24 is returned verbatim, and the model test requires 0x80 and 0xff to survive unchanged. A four-byte type is not claimed either, because the machine writes AL and not EAX.
implementation.receiver_model: a 0x25-byte opaque run with NO member declared at 0x24. The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only ({register ECX, shape R-DIRECT, offsets [36], distinct_offsets 1, max_offset 36, written_through 0, bounds_only true}), so it states where the body was seen reaching and identifies nothing; naming that byte a flag, an enabled-bit, a mode or a predicate would be a member story this evidence does not carry. 0x25 is the OBSERVED extent (the displacement plus the one byte read) and is explicitly not a claimed object size -- it is not even 4-aligned. The body's own span declares the displacement 0x24 and no member, which is the only shape the receiver record can corroborate.
implementation.dispatch_model: none, and none declared. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0; the two instructions contain no register- or memory-operand transfer; the xref export records no outgoing edge. The xref export DOES carry nine data references to this address from twelve tables, at SIX different slot indices (4, 14, 15, 26, 29, 33), which is recorded in the package header and asserted by the model test -- and is precisely why no slot boundary is declared anywhere: a single slot number cannot be right for six different ones, and the body reads no dispatch word to begin with. The model test's case G plants a dispatch-shaped table at the receiver's +0x00 whose six occupied slots would each return a different byte and count their own entry, and requires that nothing changes and nothing is entered.
implementation.callee_declarations: NONE, deliberately. The complete listing is two instructions and neither is a transfer, `callees` is empty, `external_callees` is unavailable, and the model test therefore has no callee observer. The reference package for a nearby VA declares four extern callees because its body makes four calls; declaring even one here would be inventing a transfer the bytes do not contain. What stands in for the observer is a byte-level receiver snapshot taken on both sides of every call, and the decoy dispatch table's invocation counter.

mechanics.body_shape: Two instructions, four bytes, no frame, no branch, no call, no store. The entire effect of the body is one byte load out of the receiver.

instruction_1.reading: opcode 0x8A is MOV r8, r/m8. ModRM 0x41 is mod=01, reg=000 (AL), rm=001 (ECX+disp8), so the base register is ECX and the disp8 that follows is 0x24. It is a LOAD: there is no store instruction anywhere in the body, and abi_derived.receiver records written_through 0.

instruction_2.reading: A bare RET with no immediate. `C2 nn nn` would be 3 bytes and could not fit beside a 3-byte load in a 4-byte body, and the byte at this address is C3, so the terminator form is settled by the image rather than by a length argument. 0 bytes of callee cleanup and zero stack arguments go with it.

receiver_displacement.witness_1: the instruction's own encoding: 8A 41 24 carries displacement 0x24 in its third byte
receiver_displacement.witness_2: abi_derived.receiver = {register ECX, shape R-DIRECT, offsets [36], distinct_offsets 1, max_offset 36, written_through 0, bounds_only true, present true, confidence INFERRED}; 36 decimal is 0x24
receiver_displacement.agreement: the two witnesses are the same byte of the same instruction, which is the strongest form this claim can take at this length

return_width.witness: the DESTINATION OPERAND of the only EAX definition is AL, so one byte is written. This is read off the operand, not inferred from the fact that accessors like this one tend to return flags.
return_width.not_a_zero_extension: 8A 41 24 is not 0F B6 41 24 (MOVZX EAX, byte ptr [ECX+0x24], four bytes). The compiler chose the three-byte partial-register form, so bits 8..31 of EAX are left exactly as the caller left them. Asserting a zero-extension would assert an instruction the image does not contain.

unresolved_questions: What is the byte at 0x24? The receiver record is bounds_only, so nothing here identifies it. Calling it a flag, an enabled-bit, a mode, an is-editable bit or a validity bit would be a member story the evidence does not carry, and the model deliberately names no member. Settling it needs either an SDK declaration for this slot (the SDK tree is not present in this environment; the committed vtables export carries sdk=false for this entry) or a runtime trace that shows what sets the byte.

What is the C++ spelling of the one-byte return -- bool, unsigned char or std::uint8_t? The three compile to the same three bytes and the machine cannot choose between them. std::uint8_t is declared as the least committal option; this is a source-side choice and not a verified type. The validator agrees on the WIDTH (WIDTH_1_IN_EAX) and explicitly not on the spelling.

Is the value's domain {0, 1} or 0..255? Nothing in these two instructions masks anything, and both direct callers are domain-agnostic: 0x00adfeb2 stores the raw byte, and 0x00de5278's TEST AL,AL takes the same branch for 2, 0x80 and 0xff as for 1. The model therefore returns the byte verbatim and the model test REQUIRES 0x80 and 0xff to survive, which is the opposite of asserting a boolean. A bool declaration would be an invented domain.

What do bits 8..31 of EAX hold at a real call site? The body does not set them (8A is a partial register write) and no value is claimed. Both known call sites read AL alone, so they are unobservable in this build; a third-party caller that read the full EAX would see whatever it had left there. Settling this needs either an assertion that the upper bytes are dead (not present in this build) or a caller that reads them.

Which slot, in which table, is this body's interface position? Twelve tables reference it at six different indices (4, 14, 15, 26, 29, 33), so no single index is right for all of them and none is declared. Settling it needs the class hierarchy these tables belong to; the committed export records the 0x013f7cc0 family as namespace 'unattributed' with sdkCount 0.

What class is this receiver? The target record carries subsystem 'Sporepedia' and cluster 'sporepedia-online', and the tables this body sits in have SDK-named Sporepedia::cSPAssetDataOTDB neighbours -- but THIS entry is sdk=false and unnamed, so the class is not claimed and the type is spelled SporepediaByteRecord as a shape only.

The persisted ABI record's calling convention lists __fastcall as a candidate alongside __thiscall and reports corroboration 'not_available'. __thiscall is the one both the persisted and derived records resolve to, and it is the one the listing supports (a base-register receiver, a bare RET, zero stack slots), but the corroboration field is empty and this package does not upgrade that to a claim beyond what the two records already say.

conditions: The original process is driven to an object of this class with the byte at 0x24 set to 0 and then to a non-zero value, and the full 32-bit EAX is captured at the return each time, to confirm that the upper three bytes are dead in practice rather than merely unobserved at the two known call sites.

A trace captures AL at 0x00adfeaa's return and at 0x00de5273's return against the receiver's byte at 0x24, to confirm the two call sites really do read AL alone and that no intervening code widens it.

A trace writes a value other than 0 or 1 to the byte at 0x24 and follows where it is read, which is the only way to settle the {0, 1} versus 0..255 domain question that neither instruction nor either caller can.
A trace identifies the object type reaching either call site, to settle the class identity and therefore the byte's name, and to resolve the six-way slot ambiguity across the twelve tables.

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. There is NO callee observer and the test says why: the body makes no transfer, so what stands in for an observer is a byte-level receiver snapshot taken on both sides of every call plus a decoy dispatch table whose six slots count their own invocations. Cases: A six byte values (0x00 0x01 0x7f 0x80 0xfe 0xff) round-trip verbatim, with 0x00 and 0x80 called out separately; B twelve candidate displacements are checked to be real decoys and then the result is required to be none of them, plus a mirror that moves only the byte at 0x24; C a four-byte EF BE AD DE pattern at 0x24..0x27 with the declared width, the machine instruction length, and a full-32-bit-register probe measurement that is DIFFERENTIAL: the probe is run twice with the receiver's address and its byte at +0x24 held fixed and only the three bytes at +0x25..+0x27 moved, and the whole return register must come back bit-identical; D the whole receiver fixture compared byte for byte before and after; E a receiver whose first word is a pointer to a second object with a different byte at 0x24; F two objects called through a trampoline so the result must follow ECX; G a dispatch-shaped table at the receiver's +0x00; H a pushed decoy word with ESP sampled either side of the return; I the full 32-bit return register with bits 0..7 asserted; J the recorded evidence constants checked against themselves.

mutation_checking.survivors: Three injected defects survived this run, and all three are EQUIVALENT mutants or invisible-by-construction rather than test gaps. (1) and (2): reading a 16-bit or a 32-bit value at 0x24 and then narrowing it back to the declared one-byte return type ('word read', 'dword read'). Because the reconstruction's return type is one byte, the compiler emits the same code for both, so no assertion about the compiled program can separate them; the differential full-register measurement in C6 does not separate them either, because a narrowed read leaves nothing of the wider value in the return register. The width claim is therefore still anchored on the two things that CAN fail: the declared return type (case C4, which kills a wider declaration) and the machine instruction length (case C5, the 3-byte 0x8A form versus the 4-byte 0F 0xB6 form). (3) a write of the SAME byte value back to +0x24, which case D cannot see because D compares bytes and the bytes are identical. This third one was previously recorded as KILLED with 7 failing checks (F1, F2, F3, H1, H5, I1, I3) -- every one of them a probe-fed check and none of them a byte comparison. That kill was an artifact of the old inline-asm probe, and it is reproducible as such: the same mutant, in the same package, under the same g++ -O0 command, reports those 7 bogus failures with the probe left as it was and SEGFAULTS as soon as one unrelated fprintf is added inside call_probe. The old probe's verdict therefore depended on its own register allocation rather than on the machine. The current trampoline returns the same verdict with and without that perturbation.
mutation_checking.known_limits: A write of the same byte value back to +0x24 would be invisible to case D, which compares bytes; only a write of a different value is refutable, and that is what the mutation run exercised. Case E's two-level refutation depends on the receiver's first word being a decoy, so in a case where that word happened to be a valid pointer to an object with the same byte, only the invocation would differ. Nothing asserts the class, the slot, the field's name or the value domain, because no evidence for any of them exists for this target. PROBE STABILITY, now measured rather than assumed: the old inline-asm probe was unsound and the recorded mutation run could not have detected it, because every recorded mutation was injected and rebuilt at -O0 only. Re-running the UNMUTATED test with the old probe at other optimisation levels shows it segfaults under g++ at -O2 and -O3 and under clang++ at -O0, -O2 and -O3 -- the gate only ever exercised -O0, which is why only the clang++ -O0 segfault was ever seen. The replacement is a hand-written top-level assembly trampoline with no operand constraints for a compiler to disagree about, and a perturbation sweep of 10 semantically neutral perturbations of call_probe (extra volatile counter, unrelated fprintf, extra unused locals, re-reading the result through a volatile, re-reading the receiver through a local, an extra trampoline call) across 2 compilers x 3 optimisation levels returns exit 0 in 54 of 54 runs, with the verdict unchanged by the perturbation.

validation.wpedantic_note: This package is NOT -Wpedantic-clean on GCC, and the cause is the prescribed calling-convention macro pattern itself rather than anything written here: GCC 16.2.1 rejects `__attribute__((thiscall))` on a non-class free function under -Wattributes, which -Wpedantic promotes, so even a two-line file containing only the prescribed #define block and a free function declaration fails. On the stricter raw-text reading the same is true: the only other literals in the span are 0x8A, 0xC3, 0x24 and code addresses, and every one of them is either in the encoding or in the listing.

This is the check that most needed auditing for this target, because the body IS present in twelve tables -- so the word 'vtable' was kept out of the function span entirely and the table fact lives in the file header and in this sidecar instead, with the reason recorded in evidence.vtable_associations_not_used_as_evidence.
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: WARN, and the WARN is the persisted record being wrong rather than the source. evidence_returns.decide DEFERS to the pre-existing string-agreement arm whenever any ABI source carries a canonical return_type/return_semantics claim, and the persisted envelope carries return_semantics 'pointer_like_in_EAX' (with no return_type at all). So the arm compares the literal string 'pointer_like_in_EAX' against the source's declared 'std::uint8_t' and warns that the type 'differs or is semantically renamed'. Had the deferral not been in force, the machine oracle would have read the AL destination operand, derived WIDTH_1_IN_EAX, computed the declared width as 1, and passed. The listing refutes 'pointer_like': the only definition of EAX is a one-byte load from the receiver, which is not a pointer load. So the warning is a known-bad machine claim being reported verbatim, and the disagreement is recorded in return_semantics.contradiction_in_the_machine_record and in known_blockers. It is reported, not chased: a source that returned a pointer to match the string would be a worse reconstruction, not a better one.

RESOLVED (2026-09-28, repair worker rp14) -- THE PROMOTION GATE SEGFAULTED AND THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The gate's model test died with SIGSEGV under clang++ -m32 while g++ -m32 exited 0. Root cause, diagnosed rather than guessed: the inline-asm probe in call_probe took four register operands, and clang's -m32 operand allocator mishandles that shape. With the "=&r" early-clobbered probe pointer clang allocates EDX, spills the pointer to -0x24(%ebp) and then NEVER RELOADS it, so the block's first "movl %%esp, 0(%[probe])" executed with whatever EDX the enclosing frame last held -- under the gate's PIE link, an address inside .text -- and the store faulted. Dropping the '&' is no better: clang then assigns the probe pointer and the call target the SAME register. It was NOT the early-clobber constraint itself, NOT the register chosen for the call target, and NOT PIE/EBX. FIX, in the model test only: the inline-asm block was replaced by a hand-written TOP-LEVEL ASSEMBLY trampoline emitted from the test TU (a file-scope __asm__ block, since the gate compiles only the .cpp and the model test), taking (target, receiver, decoy, samples) as ordinary cdecl arguments and writing ESP-before-push, ESP-after-return and the full 32-bit EAX into a caller-owned three-word block. The reconstruction (swarm_w1_005c0dd0.cpp) and the recorded constants (swarm_w1_005c0dd0_types.hpp) are BYTE-IDENTICAL to before this repair -- md5 fc19580f0412b5c1fc37bd749fdaf846 and 13f8673be358947bddaf2a400be79eb0 -- so every claim the reconstruction makes about the machine is unchanged, and no assertion was removed. The trampoline is position-independent by construction (it names no symbol; the target arrives as an argument), so it is correct under the gate's PIE link without needing a GOT base in EBX, and it keeps the samples pointer in the callee-saved EBX rather than a caller-saved register, because it makes an indirect call to a function it knows nothing about. Two further fragilities were removed on the way: the block uses NO "m" operand at all (the pushl moves ESP, so an ESP-relative memory operand would be read against the wrong ESP -- the defect another package in this corpus shipped until it fired only at -O2), and case C6's control no longer assumes the probe's entry state survives into the return. That second one was a second, latent bug the segfault was hiding: the old C6 zeroed EAX in the probe and asserted bits 8..31 == 0 afterwards, but clang -O0 compiles re_005c0dd0 as 'movl -4(%ebp),%eax; movl %eax,-8(%ebp); movl -8(%ebp),%eax; movb 36(%eax),%al' -- the receiver POINTER lands in EAX and only AL is written, so the upper bytes carried the receiver's own address (measured: 0xfffaacef for a planted 0xef) rather than the probe's zero. g++ emits 'movzbl (%eax),%eax', which zero-extends, so the old check passed there by accident and was a statement about one compiler's codegen, not about the width. C6 is now differential and needs no assumption at all about what the upper bytes contain: hold the receiver's address and its byte at +0x24 fixed, move only +0x25..+0x27, and require the entire 32-bit return register to be bit-identical. That is STRICTLY STRONGER -- it kills a word read (which the old zeroing form provably could not distinguish, as the file's own comment admits) as well as a dword read. VERIFICATION: the section-5 reproduction (clang++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -m32, static-library link via ar/ranlib, /tmp/g_test) exits 0; g++ -m32 single-command exits 0; all 12 combinations of {g++, clang++} x {-O0, -O2, -O3} x {single-command, static-library} exit 0; and the link was also checked with -no-pie, -pie, -fPIE and -fPIC -no-pie, all exit 0. A perturbation sweep of 10 semantically neutral changes to call_probe returns exit 0 in 54 of 54 runs, which the old probe could not do: the old probe reports 7 bogus probe-fed failures for one mutant with no extra code and SEGFAULTS for the same mutant with one unrelated fprintf added. The 18-mutation suite was re-run under both compilers: 17 KILLED, 1 SURVIVED (the same-byte write-back, which case D cannot see by construction and which known_limits already documented), plus the 2 documented equivalent width mutants, which still survive under both compilers as recorded.
